Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond.text: These fifteen conditions concern shared fields, derivatives, matrices and uniform bounds. A checking program must separately prove that its decoded data satisfy all of them.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla.text: The inequalities leave the numerical constants and the parameter family unspecified. The decimal bounds in the digest are arithmetic consequences of the paper’s chosen constants, rather than verified margins for a supplied instance.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert.text: The cell conditions yield a certificate after choosing a sufficiently large common decay bound. The argument also uses the established field, offset, reference-error and adjoint reduction results.

Breakdown.Cert.HH.text: The forcing is represented as a square-integrable time-periodic solenoidal Fourier field. The Leray projection and the physical representation identify the part of a physical forcing that acts on solenoidal tests.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.AtProfile.coerci.text: Absorbing the reference-field error divides the L² and pin constants by 1−ϑ and the row weights by (1−ϑ)². The resulting estimate applies at the approximate profile itself.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedBordered.text: The finite-dimensional identity can be added and subtracted inside the compact perturbation. Thus the full bordered operator, including the force and pin blocks, has the Fredholm form needed to deduce surjectivity from injectivity.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal..text: This result retains a continuous periodic curve of gradients in the homogeneous energy space. Taking its squared norm gives the continuous scalar enstrophy used in the integrated energy identity.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointEnclosureH.text: The adjoint enclosure is proved after setting the multiplier weight to one. The preceding rescaling of force fields and coefficients transports a general positive multiplier weight to this normalization.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointPairingHol.text: At zero perturbation, the adjoint-defect condition annihilates every gradient forcing. Hence the adjoint equals its solenoidal projection, which makes its pairing with an equation modulo gradients well defined.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol.text: The pin target and every residual pairing against a compact solenoidal test depend continuously on the parameter. The argument needs no strong continuity of a chosen unprojected residual in the full forcing norm.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol.text: Parameter selection is carried out after reference-field absorption and multiplier normalization. At that stage the reference and approximate fields agree, the multiplier weight is one, and both transfer shifts vanish.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH.text: Uniqueness holds for the bounded nonlinear corrections at one fixed parameter after normalization. It does not select a unique parameter or a unique periodic profile among all solutions.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldLimitHolds_of.text: The limit argument passes nonlinear bounded corrections to a correction at the limiting parameter. The paper instead passes linear solves indexed by an independent quadratic-force variable to a limit.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldMapsToHolds_o.text: At a fixed parameter, the nonlinear update preserves both the weighted correction radius and the gradient-supremum budget. The paper organizes its bounds as a simultaneous map of the parameter and an independent forcing variable.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_.text: The gradient lower bound rules out a corrected field that vanishes almost everywhere in space and time. After choosing its smooth representative, this yields pointwise nontriviality.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel.text: The construction adds the selected correction to the approximate profile and uses its parameter-dependent period. Its final existence conclusion omits the chosen parameter, pins and correction bounds.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedStiffEnclosureHol.text: The complementary-coordinate estimate is proved after multiplier normalization. Combining it with the approximate-field offset gives the weighted-ball part of the parameter enclosure.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of.text: The bound uses the actual selected period divided by m, and initially controls the essential supremum of the gradient norm. The forcing enters through its integrated L² norm.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of.text: The enstrophy identity is integrated over a time interval and uses a continuous periodic scalar representative. Its differential form holds wherever that scalar representative is differentiable.

Breakdown.Cert.heldDist.text: The distance combines the weighted correction norm and a scaled essential gradient supremum. Closedness of the bounded correction class and the required limit properties are established before applying the contraction argument.

Breakdown.Cert.productBoundHolds_of.text: The product estimate controls both the physical convection field and its solenoidal projection. It uses the essential time supremum, which agrees with the ordinary supremum for the continuous homogeneous-space representative.

Breakdown.Cert.sizeZ.text: The joint norm here uses multiplier weight one. Rescaling the force fields and their coefficients restores the general weight ω, while retaining the physical spatial weight w.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun.text: The pivot argument gives a positive subspace for the root form. Positivity of the total leaf form on that same subspace follows by the separate tree lower bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.text: Telescoping retains the root-front quadratic form together with the pivot gains and negative column squares. A nonnegative root front, positive pivot coverage and a bound on the number of columns are additional inputs to positivity.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.stateTerm.text: The auxiliary directions may form the graph (Lu,u), and some physical coordinates may be ignored when the form is independent of them. The dimension condition is applied after accounting for those coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeParam.text: The symmetry order is a natural-number parameter, with positivity required by the validity conditions elsewhere. Neither the intended value 19 nor the choice m=2 is selected by these data alone.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB.text: The angular estimates hold almost everywhere for the Fourier components of weak perturbations. Besides the two displayed bounds, the result also controls curl by its gradient and relates curl energy to gradient energy.

Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun.text: The exterior argument distinguishes ray exteriors from a square exterior. The latter also needs zero azimuthal frequency and the relevant reflection symmetry, so the scalar Hardy inequality is only part of the hypothesis.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.text: The phase uses time frequency 2ι₂−ι₁ and azimuthal frequency ksym ι₁. These correspond to θ and φ in the digest; the height ratio uses the third Cartesian coordinate.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.RowMultiplierIneq.text: The multiplier inequality allows general positive coercivity and nonnegative pin coefficients. The values 3/50 and 1000 are the paper’s specialization of this algebra.

Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.rec_.text: The forward recurrence keeps the homogeneous term generated by the initial value. On the stable component, that term records the stable part introduced by the compactly supported transversal.

Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.tail.text: The tail series includes powers of Θ because its forcing sequence has been divided by the desired decay factor. Its inverse already acts through the exceptional projection.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect.text: The approximate residual uses a weak Hessian and a pressure-gradient representative orthogonal to solenoidal tests. A globally classical Hessian and a chosen scalar pressure are not required at this stage.

Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds.text: Decay is proved from a similarity integral equation through weighted kernel bounds and derivative estimates. The result also controls the pressure gradient; it does not invoke Chae–Wolf as an external hypothesis.

Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileE.text: The public implication retains existence of a smooth profile. The smoothing theorem preserves velocity identity for a specified mild orbit, while further transport is needed to recover the original correction, parameter, pins and bounds.

Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_ho.text: The paper’s proof passes from $L^6$ to $L^{12}$ and then $L^\infty$. The formal construction obtains a smooth representative using Fourier estimates, local mild-solution smoothing and overlapping time intervals.

Breakdown.Freq.X.text: The homogeneous energy space is represented by a closed solenoidal subspace of Fourier L². A continuous velocity map and the gradient-norm identities connect it to physical L⁶ fields with square-integrable gradient.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact.text: The compactness proof truncates frequencies, proves total boundedness of the truncated images and controls their high-frequency tail. The Rellich argument preceding the link is the paper’s physical-space explanation.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact_holds.text: The stated compactness result restricts the coefficient to a dense space of compact solenoidal tests. The paper’s extension to every coefficient in X also uses the bilinear norm bound.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinX.text: The symmetric bilinear map is defined by dual pairings against smoothed tests. A separate formula identifies its heat evolution and solenoidal projection when one input is a compact solenoidal test field.

Breakdown.Freq.testDense_holds.text: Density allows the transfer argument to choose compact solenoidal initial data arbitrarily close to the profile. The formal whole-space transfer does not require the particular vector-potential cutoff displayed here.

Breakdown.Freq.trilinear_holds.text: The proof bounds the convection pairing and then uses L² and L⁶ estimates for the smoothed test. Their combination gives the three-quarter time power without stating the displayed L³/² mapping estimate as a separate result.

Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of.text: The raw parameter update is already proved to map K into itself. A nearest-point retraction is used only in proving the general compact-convex fixed-point theorem, after the enclosure obligation for this update has been met.

Breakdown.IsPerturbation.text: An admissible perturbation includes weak first and second spatial derivatives and the combined similarity transport. The Laplacian and transport are square integrable, while the separate global time-derivative and drift terms need not be.

Breakdown.MonodromyStatement.text: Each logarithmic period is subdivided until the linearized operator on every short interval has norm at most one quarter. The full-period map is the rotated product of the corresponding interval evolutions.

Breakdown.Periodic.ApproxSizes.Internal..text: The derivative estimate concerns one similarity-profile slice and gives a bound 2C/|y| away from the origin. The physical-time version also uses the similarity change of variables.

Breakdown.Periodic.R3Factor.text: With a compact solenoidal coefficient, the linear interaction factors through the velocity and gradient restricted to its support. Approximating the recurrent coefficient by such fields is a separate step.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellData.text: The restricted data contain three L² gradient columns and an L⁶ velocity. Their product norm is equivalent to the local sum of norms displayed in the digest, with fixed dimension-dependent constants.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties.text: The cutoff is supported on a fixed ball inside a unit-period cell and agrees with the core on a fixed smaller ball. The free radius in the paper’s presentation comes from translation and rescaling.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxPeriodic.text: Periodization uses the wrapped coordinate in a unit cube and a small blow-up time. The digest instead starts with a large-period torus and rescales it at the end.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxResidualSmall.text: The residual of the nth rescaled interval is at most K T¹/⁴ times its geometric decay factor. The digest expresses the corresponding smallness using a large torus period and a continuous weighted-time norm.

Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p.text: The final statement excludes global smooth solutions with periodic velocity and arbitrary smooth pressure. A moving-frame argument connects that class to the periodic-pressure solutions used in the construction.

Breakdown.Periodic.comparisonSmall.text: The comparison becomes smaller than any prescribed tolerance when the blow-up time is sufficiently small. The explicit powers of the large period in the digest are conclusions of the paper’s comparison estimates.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField.text: The cutoff is written as ηu+∇η×A. This is the product-rule expansion of curl(ηA) when curl A=u.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.text: The stated gradient estimate is convergence below any prescribed tolerance as the similarity scale shrinks. It does not retain the displayed explicit power of the cutoff radius.

Breakdown.Periodic.fieldSpace.text: The periodic Fourier space contains the constant mode as well as the solenoidal nonzero modes. It therefore differs from the mean-zero homogeneous space used in the paper’s large-period argument.

Breakdown.Periodic.freeHeatComparison.text: For each fixed compact solenoidal field, the restricted free heat discrepancy tends uniformly to zero on a bounded time window as the scale shrinks. No explicit large-period power is included in this conclusion.

Breakdown.Periodic.heatDivFreeComparison.text: The projected heat comparison gives arbitrary-tolerance convergence at small scale for a time window bounded away from zero. The proof uses Fourier integrals and lattice sums, while the paper obtains explicit powers through the Oseen kernel.

Breakdown.Periodic.rightInversePerturb.text: An operator defect of at most one half can be removed by a geometric-series inverse. The corrected right inverse has norm at most twice the original bound.

Breakdown.Periodic.shellInverseTransfer.text: The inverse transfer combines restriction, local interaction and evolution operators on rescaled time pieces. The displayed continuous-time formula is the paper’s organization of the same transfer mechanism.

Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist.text: The profile premise also requires uniform decay of the second spatial derivative and the pressure gradient. Lemmas A.5 and A.6 explain these extra requirements analytically, but no conversion from the printed hypotheses to this premise is among the linked results.

Breakdown.TransferHolds.text: The transfer chooses data in any given dense space and provides a positive-power error bound after restoring similarity scale. Smoothness, finite kinetic energy, the full corrected-data family and all quantitative clauses of Theorem 1.1 require further results.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_h.text: The weak-to-mild construction takes the required derivative, pairing and time-continuity results as hypotheses, supplied in the assembled proof. It concludes existence of a recurrent mild orbit without retaining the selected correction or its pins.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_space.text: The public whole-space result excludes a global smooth solution with one energy bound for all nonnegative times. It does not return the displayed rate or profile error for a chosen singular trajectory.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus.text: The public periodic result excludes a global smooth solution whose velocity is periodic. Its conclusion does not include the local H¹ comparison with a specified profile.

Breakdown.compactPiece_of.text: Simple coefficient paths are dense among continuous paths. Continuity in the coefficient and operator-norm closedness of compact operators extend the simple-path compactness result.

Breakdown.compactSimple_of.text: The proof removes the last ε of the integral and bounds that tail by a constant times ε¹/⁴. A compact convex hull controls the remainder for a simple coefficient path.

Breakdown.contraction.text: The nonlinear solve uses bounded sequences of normalized interval functions, with a factor θⁿ multiplying the quadratic term. The continuous weighted convolution in the digest is the paper’s route to the corresponding estimate.

Breakdown.dichotomyHolds.text: The spectral conclusion gives two separated radii, geometric bounds and surjectivity on the finite exceptional range. Choosing a decay rate between those radii gives the weighted sums in the digest.

Breakdown.exists_section.text: The bounded lift J preserves the exceptional projection and takes values in the dense test-field space. Its restriction to the finite exceptional range gives the compactly supported transversal E.

Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro.text: A certificate gives existence of a nonzero weak periodic similarity profile. The conclusion does not retain the complete same-parameter, same-correction statement with pins, symmetries and bounds from Theorem 7.1.

Breakdown.mildRegular_realization.text: The regularity theorem supplies a smooth representative with bounded energy on each fixed compact time interval. The bound by the initial energy and one bound valid on all of [0,1) are not part of this conclusion.

Breakdown.mildSmallData.text: The small-data result gives a mild solution through time one with norm at most twice the initial norm. Scaling and interval choices supply the short-time instances needed later.

Breakdown.orbitNorm_of.text: The positive lower orbit bound is proved through small-data decay, mild uniqueness and recurrence. The compact-period minimum argument in the digest is a different explanation of the same conclusion.

Breakdown.orbitSeq.text: The recurrence divides each successor by the chosen decay factor Θ. Removing that normalization gives the unweighted recurrence displayed in the digest.

Breakdown.periodicInverse.text: The inverse acts on sequences of continuous interval functions. Its first output is an exceptional coordinate e; the compactly supported initial correction is Je.

Breakdown.physicalField.text: The physical velocity is defined at terminal time one, with an arbitrary logarithmic phase. The formula with terminal time T follows by scaling time and space.

Breakdown.physicalPressure.text: The pressure is defined with terminal time one and the same logarithmic phase as the physical velocity. Its multiplicative factor is $(1-t)^{-1}$.

Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace.text: For every positive viscosity, the statement supplies smooth compact solenoidal data admitting no global smooth solution with one kinetic-energy bound for all nonnegative times. This agrees with the endpoint description in the digest.

Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus.text: For every positive viscosity, the statement supplies smooth periodic solenoidal data admitting no global smooth solution with periodic velocity. It imposes no periodicity requirement on the pressure.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert.text: The full cell conditions, together with the analytic reduction results, yield a certificate after increasing a common decay bound. This is a conditional implication and supplies no numerical instance.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceAndTorusB.text: Data satisfying all fifteen cell conditions imply both whole-space and periodic breakdown. Decoding a file and proving that its contents satisfy those conditions remain separate obligations.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.AtProfile.coerci.text: The estimate transfers reference coercivity to the approximate profile by dividing by 1−ϑ. Multiplying through by that positive factor gives the absorbed estimate in the digest.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedHeldCont.text: After normalization and with zero pin difference, the row bound and L² forcing bound combine into cL times the forcing norm. This is the inverse constant used for differences of corrections.
Two bordered solutions with the same target pins have a difference whose pins vanish. This is exactly the cancellation needed before applying the inverse estimate.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal..text: The result returns a continuous periodic gradient curve in the homogeneous energy space, agreeing almost everywhere with the free-inverse representative and satisfying the integrated enstrophy identity.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.HeldContracts.pr.text: The algebra bounds each bilinear contribution by cw M times the correction distance, using its weighted and scaled-supremum components. Adding them gives the factor 2cw M, once the analytic product bound is supplied.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointEnclosureH.text: The adjoint error estimate is proved after setting the multiplier weight to one. The display in the digest uses a general positive ω, reached by rescaling the force fields and their coefficients; its offset term also comes from the certificate conditions.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedBorderedInvertibl.text: After reference-field absorption and multiplier normalization, the bordered operator has a right inverse on the symmetry-invariant forcing space and is injective there. This gives the unique linear solve used at that stage of the argument.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedConvectionCompact.text: Local compactness of the free inverse and the approximate-profile decay bounds make convection after free inversion compact. This is the compact perturbation used in the bordered problem.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol.text: After normalization, the result supplies a parameter and a nonlinear correction obeying both bounds for which the approximate and correction force coefficients sum to zero. Reference-field absorption and the force rescaling prepare that normalized certificate.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHold.text: The contraction factor is 2cL cw M<1. The second scalar smallness condition supplies the supremum component of the inverse estimate, while the first makes the final factor strictly smaller than one.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH.text: At each fixed parameter, the normalized nonlinear problem has a unique correction within the class satisfying the equation, pins and both budgets. The conclusion makes no uniqueness claim for the selected parameter or all recurrent profiles.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldLimitHolds_of.text: A sequence of bounded nonlinear corrections at convergent parameters has a subsequence whose multipliers converge to those of a correction at the limiting parameter. Fixed-parameter uniqueness then yields continuity.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_.text: The strict approximate-gradient lower bound and the correction budget rule out a corrected field vanishing almost everywhere. This is the nontriviality assertion needed before smoothing.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedMultiplierContinu.text: The total multiplier depends continuously on the parameter in K. The proof uses compactness of bounded corrections and their uniqueness at each fixed parameter.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel.text: The conclusion gives existence of a normalized-time weak profile. It omits the chosen parameter, its period, the correction identity, pins and quantitative bounds retained together by Theorem 7.1.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedStiffEnclosureHol.text: The theorem bounds the correction multiplier on the coordinates outside J after normalization. The approximate-field offset and the final weighted-ball inclusion come from additional certificate inequalities.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of.text: The gradient-supremum estimate has the same weight, period divided by m, quadratic-form and forcing coefficients as the display. It initially uses an essential supremum, equal to the ordinary supremum for the continuous homogeneous-space representative.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of.text: The statement gives an interval-integrated identity for a continuous periodic scalar enstrophy. The pointwise derivative formula in the digest is its differential form at times of differentiability.

Breakdown.Cert.freeInvHolds_of.text: The result supplies the free inverse and bounds its squared Laplacian norm plus one quarter of its squared gradient norm by the squared forcing norm. The assembled proof supplies the propagator and weak-derivative prerequisites.

Breakdown.Cert.productBoundHolds_of.text: The bilinear estimate yields the displayed quadratic bound with the same cw. It uses the essential gradient supremum, which becomes the ordinary supremum for a continuous representative; applying it twice gives the quadratic-difference estimate.

Breakdown.Cert.productSubHolds_of.text: The quadratic difference is the sum of the two displayed bilinear terms. The equality holds for the solenoidal projections and almost everywhere for their physical representatives.

Breakdown.Cert.rowNormHolds.text: Orthonormal row fields with weights at most c₀² give [F]≤c₀‖F‖H. The result also gives subadditivity and invariance under changing the sign of F.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.tailGainHold.text: Valid cell bases and mode relations give the spectral lower bounds for polynomial remainders. The radial, height and angular gains control the derivative tails used by the reduction.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesPiv.text: The conditions require every coordinate to have a positive pivot, a nonnegative root front and no more bad columns than auxiliary coordinates. These are exactly the hypotheses of the positivity step.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun.text: The root form is positive on a subspace of at least the physical-coordinate dimension, obtained from the common kernel of bad-column pairings. The separate tree bound transfers positivity to the total leaf form.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.text: The telescoping inequality retains the root-front quadratic form. The pivot-minus-column formula displayed in the digest additionally uses its nonnegativity before dropping that term.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.stateTerm.text: The terminal theorem permits auxiliary directions of the form (Lu,u) and physical coordinates on which the form is independent. The digest explains the simpler pure-free case; the general dimension condition accounts for both extensions.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldDiver.text: For valid represented fields, the mode smoothness and divergence identities imply zero divergence at every point and time. The assembled cell construction supplies those facts.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldWeakS.text: The represented piecewise Hessian is the weak second derivative of the assembled field, under the two mode-family regularity conditions. Arbitrary unmatched piecewise data are outside the assertion.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.jetSplineJ.text: A valid jet spline has the prescribed matching derivatives across its cell joins. This supplies the compatibility needed for the piecewise derivative formulas.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo.text: The exterior hypothesis combines the scalar Hardy test with a permitted exterior geometry, mode conditions, coefficient floors and ceilings, and a positive Hardy constant. The displayed scalar inequality alone does not express the full hypothesis.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB.text: The result includes the two displayed velocity and gradient inequalities almost everywhere for weak Fourier modes, and additionally the curl-gradient inequality. The surrounding sentence correctly supplies the almost-everywhere interpretation.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua.text: The angular bounds and admissible coefficients reduce the mode density to a two-variable quadratic form with nonnegative diagonal terms and the stated discriminant bound. The auxiliary shift is a coefficient, independent of physical time.

Breakdown.CertCell.cellLayerParts_closed.text: The assembled analytic cell results establish the trace, row-range, remainder and gauge steps used in the reduction. Numerical entry conditions remain assumptions when the final perturbation bound is applied.

Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun.text: The integrated exterior inequality follows from the full geometric and mode-dependent exterior hypothesis. Its scalar Hardy absorption test is the one displayed in the digest.

Breakdown.CertCell.rowRestClause_closed.text: The cell, shape, tree and entry conditions yield the row-rest inequality for every admissible perturbation. The perturbation is not confined to the numerical approximation space.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.ExtendedCoerciveC.text: The inverse estimate quantifies over every admissible perturbation, multiplier and square-integrable forcing representative. It therefore includes unresolved modes and exterior regions.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.extendedCoerciveC.text: The multiplier norm and pairing inequalities imply the universal a priori bound with generic coercivity and pin constants. The numerical coefficients in the digest are one specialization.

Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds.text: For a smooth recurrent orbit satisfying the profile integral equation, the result gives exactly the velocity derivatives of orders zero through two and the pressure-gradient powers stated in the digest. Its weighted-kernel proof differs from the cited paper route.

Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_ho.text: The smoothing theorem gives smooth velocity and pressure for a specified mild orbit and retains equality of the velocity almost everywhere in space at every time. It reaches this conclusion by a different proof from the printed bootstrap.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact.text: The conclusion is compactness for compact solenoidal test coefficients, proved through Fourier truncation and total boundedness. This matches the passage explicitly describing that proof route.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact_holds.text: For a coefficient in the dense test-field space and positive time, the bilinear operator is compact. This matches the explicitly restricted phrase, while the earlier claim for arbitrary coefficients requires approximation.

Breakdown.Freq.bilin_holds.text: The bilinear operator exists for every positive time and satisfies the exact $C\tau^{-3/4}$ product bound in $X$. These are the construction and estimate used in the digest.

Breakdown.Freq.dilation_holds.text: The result includes the quarter-power norm identity and also the dilation composition and heat-commutation laws. The extra conclusions strengthen the isolated norm identity.

Breakdown.Freq.rotation_holds.text: The norm equality is supplied by the construction of rotation as an isometry. The linked theorem itself identifies its Fourier action and its commutation with heat and dilation.

Breakdown.Freq.testDense_holds.text: The result supplies ordinary density and simultaneous graph-norm approximation by compact solenoidal tests. The digest uses only ordinary density.

Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of.text: The two enclosures, continuity, nonzero coordinate scales and an invertible frame give a raw self-map of K and a parameter with zero total multiplier. Non-strict inclusions and sets with empty interior are allowed.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties.text: The result gives smoothness, zero divergence, fixed compact support and core agreement for the unit-period cutoff. The paper writes the same construction with a freely chosen physical radius, requiring a scale change for comparison.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.text: The formal conclusion makes the squared gradient error smaller than any tolerance at sufficiently small similarity scale. The digest displays a quantitative power of the large cutoff radius.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffMassBound.text: The formal squared-mass bound is proportional to $(T-t)^{-1/2}$ for the rescaled cutoff. The digest uses the corresponding physical-radius bound, whose relation requires changing scale.

Breakdown.Periodic.glueMild.text: Compatible exact interval solutions glue to an exact periodic mild solution. Smoothness and the final breakdown assertion are supplied by later results.

Breakdown.Periodic.homotopyCurl.text: The radial potential has curl equal to any smooth solenoidal input field. The digest uses the case with centre zero at each fixed time.

Breakdown.Periodic.rightInversePerturb.text: A sufficiently small operator perturbation admits an exact bounded right inverse, with an explicit factor-two norm bound when the defect is at most one half. This is the inverse step in the torus correction.

Breakdown.Periodic.seqPerturbation.text: The nonlinear interval construction absorbs the approximate residual into the correction and returns exact mild equations. The residual is therefore removed from the final equation.

Breakdown.TransferHolds.text: The transfer selects initial data in the supplied dense space and retains a quantitative rescaled error estimate. This agrees with the deliberately limited description of that intermediate result.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_h.text: After the stated analytic prerequisites are supplied, the weak profile gives a continuous recurrent mild orbit. The conclusion is existential and does not contain the paper’s intermediate $L^{12}$ estimate.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_space.text: The public result covers every positive viscosity and excludes global uniformly finite-energy smooth solutions, but omits the constructed trajectory, blow-up rate and profile error. Its profile hypothesis also contains additional decay requirements, so its full scope differs from Theorem 1.1.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus.text: The public periodic result covers every positive viscosity and allows arbitrary smooth pressure with periodic velocity. It omits the terminal time, two-sided rate and local H¹ comparison and assumes the profile with additional decay.

Breakdown.compactPiece_of.text: The proof extends compactness from simple coefficient paths to all continuous coefficient paths by density and operator-norm closure. This is the general time-dependent coefficient step described in the digest.

Breakdown.compactSimple_of.text: For a simple coefficient path, the proof removes an ε terminal interval, bounds that tail by a quarter power, and treats the remaining integral through a compact convex hull. The next compactness result supplies the density extension.

Breakdown.contraction.text: The nonlinear theorem solves a quadratic equation on bounded sequences of rescaled interval functions and bounds the initial correction. The digest presents the corresponding continuous weighted-time contraction.

Breakdown.decayFieldDilate_holds.text: Positive dilation preserves a smooth solenoidal field and its velocity and gradient decay. This supplies incompressibility after the similarity change; the physical momentum equation is a separate result.

Breakdown.dichotomyHolds.text: The spectral result gives a real finite-rank commuting projection, separated radii, stable and exceptional power bounds, and surjectivity on the exceptional range. The displayed weighted sums follow at an intermediate decay rate.

Breakdown.exists_section.text: The conclusion returns a bounded lift J preserving the exceptional projection and taking values in the dense test-field space. The finite-dimensional isomorphic transversal E is obtained by restricting J to the exceptional range.

Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro.text: The public conclusion is existence of a nonzero weak periodic profile. It does not retain the selected parameter, period, correction, pins and quantitative bounds of Theorem 7.1; this comparison concerns the conclusion only.

Breakdown.monodromy.text: The theorem gives compactness of the rotated full-period product minus its free product and bounds the latter by exp(−S/4). It is the compact-perturbation assertion after assembling the short intervals.

Breakdown.orbitBound.text: A continuous recurrent orbit has a uniform upper norm bound, including recurrence up to an isometry. This is the upper half of the orbit comparison used in the digest.

Breakdown.orbitNorm.text: A nonzero recurrent mild orbit has one strictly positive lower bound for all its slice norms. This matches the orbit-level lower bound stated in the digest.

Breakdown.periodicInverse.text: The bounded inverse acts on normalized sequences of continuous interval functions and returns an exceptional coordinate e. The paper’s continuous formulation writes the lifted initial correction Je as γ.

Breakdown.physicalMild_unconditional.text: Under the smooth-profile premise and continuity of its homogeneous-space representative, the physical profile satisfies the mild equation on every compact interval before terminal time one. This is the weak-to-mild conversion used in the digest.

Breakdown.physicalMomentum_holds.text: The theorem proves the viscosity-one momentum identity at terminal time one under the profile with its additional decay assumptions and the derivative-calculus results. The general terminal-time formula and incompressibility require the accompanying scale and divergence steps.

Breakdown.rowNorm.text: The row seminorm is the weighted Euclidean norm of finitely many forcing pairings, exactly the quantity used in the digest. Its bound by the forcing norm is proved separately.

Breakdown.supBoundFactor.text: The constant is exactly $(4\pi\sqrt{w^*})^{-1/2}$ after simplifying the nested square roots. It is the same coefficient as in the displayed product estimate.

Breakdown.transferHolds_of_dichotomy.text: The theorem assembles the nearby-data mild trajectory and positive-power rescaled error estimate from the spectral splitting. Smooth physical representatives and kinetic-energy bounds require the subsequent regularity results.

Breakdown.varConstIntegral.text: For bounded continuous inputs on a compact interval, the result gives integrability, a quarter-power norm bound and continuity of the Duhamel term. These are the properties used at the linked step.

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
